title: Access Assurance PRD — Identity & Crypto Acceptance Checklist and Clarifications
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: PRD addendum that captures detailed requirements, acceptance criteria, and a signoff checklist for SSO (SAML/OIDC), RBAC role mapping, and KMS/HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated deployments. This ticket clarifies scope changes requested during compliance reviews and defines concrete test evidence required to close onboarding gates for enterprise customers.
scope_changes: Narrowed initial rollout to include only SAML2.0 IdP connectors + OIDC for token exchange; postponed SAML IdP-initiated single logout (SLO) to a follow-up ticket.
Added customer-managed KMS (CMK) integration for AWS KMS and a separate HSM-backed key option for on-prem bundles.
RBAC: Deliver role templates (Admin, Operator, Auditor, Viewer) and mapping guide rather than a full RBAC UI in first iteration.
Audit logging retention bumped from 90 days to 7 years for enterprise compliance; implement tiered retention policy in the console as a follow-up.
Introduced offline key escrow process for air-gapped customers; implementation deferred to Q3 pilot.
decisions: Use SAML 2.0 (IdP metadata upload) as the canonical enterprise SSO mechanism for private deployments; OIDC supported for modern IdPs and service-to-service flows.
KMS integration will support both 'bring-your-own-key' (BYOK) via customer-managed CMKs and an HSM-backed operator key with quorum controls.
Audit logs must be cryptographically tamper-evident (append-only storage with hash chaining) and exportable in bundled evidence form for audits.
RBAC model will be role-based with optional attribute mapping (ABAC-lite) for group-to-role translation on SAML assertion.
Rotate operator wrapping keys automatically every 90 days with a documented emergency-rotation drill and recovery runbook.
Operator separation: no single operator role can perform both key rotation and audit log deletion; enforcement via RBAC and KMS policies.
Acceptance criteria must include live integration tests against a customer IdP emulator and against an HSM simulator for deterministic verification.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end SAML flow: SP-initiated login, assertion validation (aud, exp, issuer), group-to-role mapping applies correctly for three sample identity providers.
OIDC token exchange: refresh and introspection endpoints validate and respect audience/scopes; token revocation verified.
RBAC templates: Admin/Operator/Auditor/Viewer templates exist in the console and map to expected permission sets; at least one scoped role-binding test passes.
KMS BYOK: Customer-supplied CMK can be registered, used for envelope encryption of model artifacts, and key usage audited (create, use, rotate, revoke).
HSM-backed keys: HSM simulator exercises quorum signing; automatic rotation performed and validated by recovery test.
Audit logs: retention policy enforced, logs are immutably stored with cryptographic hashes, and a 3rd-party audit export contains the required fields (timestamp, actor, operation, resource, outcome).
Operational runbooks: documented runbook for key compromise, including notification steps, rotation procedure, and customer impact assessment.
Compliance evidence package: generated bundle contains configuration snapshot, IdP metadata, key registration events, RBAC mappings, and sample audit export for a defined period.
Smoke SLOs: auth latency under 200ms for 95th percentile in private deployment baseline; key operations below 1s when cached and within acceptable SLA when cold.
Recovery drill: simulated key rotation recovery completes without data loss and is validated by a secondary verification script.

test_plan: Automated test harness that runs against IdP emulator for 5 canonical IdP configurations (Okta, AzureAD, OneLogin, Ping, Generic SAML).
HSM simulator acceptance suite that validates quorum signing, rotation, and offline recovery behavior.
End-to-end smoke tests executed by CI against a dedicated staging environment that mirrors private deployment network policies.
Manual compliance acceptance: run the audit export and verify fields with Legal for two sample time windows.
Chaos test: simulate network partition between control plane and KMS to validate fallback/alerts and ensure no silent data corruption.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (staging): Deploy to internal staging with IdP emulator + HSM simulator; complete full test plan.
Phase 1 (pilot customers): Onboard up to 3 enterprise pilots with BYOK only; collect evidence packages and iterate.
Phase 2 (wider rollout): Enable HSM-backed option and RBAC templates for all private deployments; provide migration guide.
Phase 3 (general availability): Release console controls for retention tiers and evidence export; publish compliance whitepaper.
Rollout gates: each phase requires signoffs per the signoff_checklist and zero critical security findings.
risks_mitigations: Risk: IdP variety causes mapping edge cases. Mitigation: provide a mapping debugger and a set of canonical example mappings for customers.
Risk: Key compromise during rotation. Mitigation: staged rotation with escrowed wrapped keys + drill and manual rollback steps.
Risk: Audit export size and performance for long retention. Mitigation: tiered retention storage and on-demand export worker with throttling.
Risk: Air-gapped installs cannot access cloud KMS. Mitigation: provide HSM operator package and offline key import tooling.
notes: Keep SLOs conservative for pilot customers; we can tighten after telemetry from pilot runs.
Legal requested examples of export format for GDPR data subject requests — added to test plan.
Coordinate with Sales for pilot selection: choose customers representing both cloud and air-gapped needs.
Follow-on tickets: full SLO tuning (PM-37800), SLO alerting playbook (ENG-42990), and SLO docs for customers (PM-38001).
